result.title: From Outranking Flow Scores to Linear Programs: Group Decision Making in PROMETHEE II
result.comment: 15 pages; 1 figure; to be published in Algorithmic Decision Theory, 9th International Conference, ADT 2026, Lecture Notes in Computer Science
result.summary: We study inverse and consensus analysis for PROMETHEE II ranking problems when the performance table is fixed. Existing approaches in PROMETHEE-based sensitivity and consensus analysis usually focus on deviations of criteria weights while treating preference functions as fixed. Nevertheless both sets of parameters jointly determine the outranking flow scores. We introduce a linear reparametrization of the PROMETHEE II net flow scores based on weighted preference increments over the observed differences of performances. This representation yields a linear expression of the net flows and clarifies how weights and preference functions interact. Building on this result, we derive linear optimization models for three settings: minimizing weight deviations while allowing preference functions to vary; minimizing deviations over the full set of preference parameters; and multiple decision-maker consensus analysis (with objectives based either on total deviation or on the maximal individual deviation to promote fairness). An illustrative example shows that allowing preference functions to vary can dramatically change the inverse-analysis conclusions obtained from weight-only models, and that the proposed group formulations distinguish efficient consensuses from fairer ones.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究固定性能表下 PROMETHEE II 排序的逆分析与共识分析，对净流分数做基于加权偏好增量的线性重参数化，并据此建立三类线性优化模型：允许偏好函数变化时的权重偏差最小化、全部偏好参数偏差最小化，以及多决策者共识（按总偏差或最大个体偏差）。
